key_fields.sql: select z.borough, count(*) as touches from lake.trips t join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid group by z.borough order by z.borough
key_fields.claim: An OR inside the JOIN condition cannot use a hash join; the engine falls back to a nested-loop style join, which is far more expensive than two equi-joins. (matched: inner join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid)

value.sql: SELECT z.Borough, COUNT(*) AS touches FROM lake.trips t JOIN ops.zones z ON z.LocationID = t.PULocationID GROUP BY z.Borough UNION ALL SELECT z.Borough, COUNT(*) AS touches FROM lake.trips t JOIN ops.zones z ON z.LocationID = t.DOLocationID GROUP BY z.Borough ORDER BY z.Borough
value.change_summary: Split the OR join into two separate equi-joins with UNION ALL to enable hash join optimization, then aggregate by Borough.
value.risk_notes: Trips where PULocationID = DOLocationID and both match a zone will be counted twice (once per join), matching the original OR-join behavior because the original join also produces two rows for such trips due to matching both conditions with the unique zones table.
